messages:
Alex Chen: FYI I ran a couple of nsys profiles on the new batching path to investigate the perf regression reported yesterday. Initial finding: lots of GPU memcpy stalls during hotpath for KV cache warmups.

Priya Kapoor: Interesting — are these H2D or peer copies?

Alex Chen: Mostly H2D and some D2H for checkpoints. Also a surprising number of cudaMemcpy calls flagged as "pageable" which caused CPU-side serialization. Timeline snippet from nsys: 

```
GPU memcpy H2D (pageable): 4.8 ms  <-- repeated per request
GPU memcpy H2D (pinned): 0.9 ms
Kernel attention: 1.2 ms
KV cache read kernel: 0.6 ms
Host->Device queue stalls: visible aligned with memcpy events
```

Ben R.: That matches what I saw in perfetto traces: big gaps between enqueue and kernel start when we touch new KV pages. Might be missing cudaHostAlloc / pinned pool usage in the batcher.

Maya S.: Do we know which code path is allocating these buffers? Could be the prefix cache path we added for dynamic prompts. 

Alex Chen: Yes — the cache-refill path allocates a new staging buffer per request today (malloc then cudaMemcpy). If it's pageable, driver does an internal pinned copy which blocks CPU and costs extra copy -> stalls the whole stream.

Priya Kapoor: Repro steps / commands you used? Share so I can run locally.

Alex Chen: Ran with nsys and nvprof variants: 
```
nsys profile -f true -o /tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,nvtx python -m perf.runner --config=grpc-batcher --profile-name=kv-warmup
nvprof --unified-memory-profiling off --print-gpu-trace python -m perf.runner --bench kv_warmup
# perfetto: record host+gpu and upload to cloud link
```

Ben R.: Perf numbers: with pageable buffers avg batch H2D was ~4.2ms; switching to cudaHostAlloc (pinned) reduced to ~0.8-1.0ms but allocation churn increased tail latencies due to host alloc cost. Suggest pre-allocated pinned pool.

Maya S.: Could NVLink peer copies be better for Dedicated nodes where model & KV are on different GPUs? I saw some peer-copy spikes.

Alex Chen: Good call — on DGX nodes NVLink peer-to-peer copies measured ~0.3-0.5ms for a 2MB region vs PCIe ~1.7-2.5ms. But we saw unexpected serialized peer copies when PCIe fallback occurred (peer-to-peer not enabled or different numa). Trace showed 'cuMemcpyPeerAsync' chained and waiting on PCIe transfers.

Priya Kapoor: So root causes: pageable allocations on host causing pageable stalls + fallback to PCIe for some peer copies due to topology constraints.

Ben R.: Fix plan: 1) change KV warmup to use a pinned staging buffer pool (cudaHostAlloc with cudaHostAllocPortable | cudaHostAllocMapped?) 2) add topology check at startup to prefer cudaMemcpyPeer for NVLink neighbors, fallback metrics logged 3) batcher: allocate per-worker pinned slab instead of per-request 4) add nsys nvtx markers around memcpy + kernel to make regressions visible in alerts.

Maya S.: For (1) we should implement a lock-free ring buffer for pinned pages to avoid expensive host allocs at runtime. Also limit pool size per-GPU to keep host memory sane (e.g., 512MB per GPU).

Alex Chen: Agreed. I prototyped a pool: warmup cost ~60ms at cold start for 512MB, but per-request alloc goes to ~0.05ms. That removes the pageable stalls. 

Priya Kapoor: Any perf regressions remaining after that?

Alex Chen: After pool + topology checks: average token latency dropped 12-18% on our 2k-seq stress tests. We still see tail spikes in multi-tenant cases when two GPUs try to pin simultaneously — likely contention on driver page-pinning resources.

Ben R.: Could be due to host-side NUMA. Add numa-bind to pinned allocations or use cudaHostAllocPortable? Also instrument with /proc/interrupts and iommu stats when reproducing.

Maya S.: I'll add a perfetto template for us to capture both host perf counters and GPU memcpy lanes. Also will add a dashboard cell in Console: "H2D pageable stalls" flagged when mean memcpy/prefill > 2ms.

infra-bot: deploy-batcher-pr-#981 merged to staging :rocket: (deployed to staging/dedicated-1)

Alex Chen: After deploy I ran a quick nvprof on staging: pinned pool + peer preference reduced average batch prefill time from 3.9ms -> 0.95ms; peer copies on NVLink neighbors are 3-5x faster than PCIe fallback.

Priya Kapoor: Nice. Let's also add a regression test: run nsys profile during CI perf job and assert memcpy H2D percentile < 2ms for our sample workload.

Ben R.: One more gotcha: when using mapped pinned memory (cudaHostAllocMapped) we saw one driver bug on some OS kernels that caused rare hangs. I vote for portable pinned + explicit cudaMemcpyAsync to device instead of relying on mapping.

Maya S.: I'll draft the PR with pinned-pool, topology-aware memcpy, and NVTX instrumentation. Tagging @Priya for CI test changes. :eyes:

Priya Kapoor: LGTM. Add a short HOWTO in eng-runtime docs: "Diagnosing H2D stalls with nsys & perfetto" with sample commands and expected timeline screenshots.

Alex Chen: I'll paste the nsys snippet into the doc once we have perfetto link. For now, here's the quick checklist we used: 
- run nsys with --trace=cuda,nvtx and check for long "memcpy H2D (pageable)" events
- if present, confirm host alloc usage in code path -> switch to pinned pool
- test peer-to-peer availability (cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer) and prefer cuMemcpyPeerAsync on NVLink neighbors
- instrument NVTX around memcpy + cache ops for CI detection

Maya S.: Great. We'll monitor staging and roll to dedicated after 24-48h of no regressions.

Alex Chen: Thanks all — will open the PR w/ benchmark numbers and nsys captures. Ping me if you want to reproduce locally; I left a small script in /infra/perf/kv_warmup_profile.sh

Priya Kapoor: Thanks Alex :clap:

Ben R.: Awesome work, this should materially reduce tail latency for many workloads. :thumbsup:
